headline: President Clinton amended an earlier order that set up a White House committee on the International Labor Organization.
what_it_does: This order changes Executive Order 12216, which created the President's Committee on the International Labor Organization (ILO). The ILO is a United Nations agency that deals with worker rights and labor standards around the world. The title does not say exactly what was changed, such as who sits on the committee or what its duties are.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the President's Committee on the International Labor Organization
who_it_affects.how: The rules that govern their committee were changed, though the specific changes are not described in the available information.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed August 27, 1999; the exact effective date is not stated in the available information.
